reviews.title: Disappointing Experience and Lack of Transparency
reviews.text:
I genuinely enjoyed using Feeld and appreciated having a platform designed for open-minded people seeking meaningful connections. Unfortunately, my experience with their customer support and account moderation has been extremely disappointing.

My account was banned without a clear explanation of which specific community guideline I allegedly violated. I submitted an appeal and requested clarification, yet I have received no meaningful explanation or transparency regarding the decision.

As a transgender woman, I’ve also experienced harassment from users who matched with me before reading my profile. Despite these experiences, I have always made an effort to treat others respectfully and follow the platform’s guidelines.

It’s frustrating that an app promoting inclusivity, authenticity, and acceptance can make users feel so dismissed when they need support. I understand the importance of community safety and moderation, but users deserve fair treatment, transparency, and a meaningful opportunity to appeal decisions.

Feeld has a great concept, but its customer support and moderation process need significant improvement. Until that changes, I cannot recommend the app.

reviews.title: Banned without explanation. Appeal ignored.
reviews.text:
Honestly, I’m really disappointed by what happened with FEELD.

When I first joined, the community felt like a dream come true. There were people from all walks of the LGBTQ+ community, including doms and subs, men, women, and trans and genderfluid people. I’m genderfluid myself, and it was refreshing to find a space where people were so open about who they were and what they were looking for. I had some great conversations, some ghosts, and the usual mix you expect from a social/dating app.

Then I took a break for about a month.

When I came back, I discovered that my account had been banned, and apparently my IP was banned as well. I have no idea why. I went through the appeal process looking for an explanation, and more than a month later I still haven’t received any meaningful response.

If you’re going to permanently ban someone’s account and prevent them from creating another one, the least you can do is tell them what they supposedly did wrong and actually respond to their appeal.

I genuinely liked the community and thought I had finally found an app where I fit in. Instead, I was locked out without an explanation and left completely in the dark.

Really disappointing experience. I expected better from FELD.

I am beyond frustrated with Feeld’s customer service.

I created my account about a month ago with the help of a friend. Immediately after paying the $50 Majestic membership fee, the app’s “bot” flagged me as fraud and blocked my account.

I went through the automated support process and sent several screenshots when I was told, “Let’s get you to a human.” Instead, I received a notice saying customer service responses were taking 1+ weeks.

I waited the week. Nothing.

I submitted another request through the support link and finally received an email on 9/16/26 acknowledging the issue and saying they were working on it. Since then? Nothing. I have followed up again and still have received no response.

So here I am, $50 out of pocket for a membership I cannot even use, with no resolution and essentially no customer service.

At this point, I simply want my $50 refunded. I have already requested that through their support system, but apparently getting a response is nearly impossible.

Feeld customer service has been incredibly disappointing. I understand that automated systems can make mistakes, but when a paying customer is incorrectly blocked, there should be a reasonable way to get the issue resolved — and certainly within a month.

The paid tier costs premium money, but real conversations are rare. I send carefully written pings and most go unanswered. After months of consistent use I have a handful of real exchanges, which is a poor return on what I've spent.

I’ve had two irrevocably bad experiences with Feeld. The takeaway is that one should be extremely careful about engaging with an app that is both extremely prone to glitches and with ineffective customer support. In the best case it will be a waste of your time only; and in the worst case you will be exposed to petty theft as well. 

1) I cannot save edits to my profile; and, hence am unable to display any information (aside from photos) on it. This is a fundamental feature of a dating app and you would think Feeld would address it urgently. However, it has been months since I raised this issue and it remains unresolved.

2) I was double-charged for an in app purchase of Pings. When I requested a refund via Apple for the duplicate charge, they issued it, but took back the Pings. Apple states it’s Feeld’s T&C that requires them to uphold this policy of automatically retracting any item purchased when issuing a refund. Obviously, this does not remedy a double-charge. I contacted Feeld support to resolve the issue, but they claimed everything was processed as expected, and refused to do anything further. In summary, a Feeld glitch resulted in money being taken from me, and there’s absolutely nothing that can be done about it (besides what recourse can be offered by my financial institution or, if need be, the courts; but, you would hope Feeld would have provided a resolution to a problem they created; particularly when it yields a financial loss).

Feeld is kind of OK, but it’s not great. As with any app like this, male users are hugely disadvantaged in terms of sheer numbers, and the app is effectively designed to make men pay. Because there are so many male users, the chances of your profile even being seen are minuscule unless you pay for an uplift, which is pricy. In the unlikely event that someone likes your profile, you have to pay to see who it is. The only way to send a ping, or direct message, is to pay for them, and they are never answered, presumably because female users are inundated with them.

All of that is perhaps not unreasonable - the gender imbalance isn’t the developers’ fault, after all, and they have to charge something to make a living. But the prices are high, and because they’re based on buying hope they function like loot boxes psychologically speaking. You can pay the “majestic” subscription, but again it is expensive and it doesn’t include an uplift. The most cynical thing, though, and the one that really makes me mark the app down, is the fact that if your majestic subscription runs out, your profile automatically gets a temporary uplift, making it more visible. That means you’re more likely to receive likes - but you can only see who they are from if you pay for another majestic subscription. This is pure manipulative behaviour that’s designed to entice people back to paying the subscription - after which of course your profile loses its uplift and sinks back into total obscurity.

reviews.text: To be fair, it was great when it’s first released. 6 months later I tried using it again and unfortunately welcomed back by the classic dating app algorithm with lots of fake profiles. It offers nothing better than tinder sadly these days.

reviews.title: Basically a subscription trap
reviews.text: I finally found a dating app where I could be myself and hopefully find someone who shares those interests openly and after seeing how many likes I was getting,  I was pretty excited to see who I could potentially match with and that’s where the fun ends. For the app to be any use you have to pay for the full upgraded version which I don’t think is fair, of course every dating app has its upgraded features but the free version should just be as exciting and I don’t think this is sadly. After swiping through so many profiles where we don’t have the same interests/goals, I came across one profile and that was my first heart sent but then I quickly realised that if they haven’t paid for the full subscription they might not see my profile, how many others are my type that are sitting in my likes that I can’t access unless I pay? Great idea for the app but not so great unless you’re willing to pay for it to be worthwhile.  Even on hinge you can see who likes you and they still have the option for people to upgrade if they wish to do so.
